# Salt Choir Structure History

How The Salt Choir has been built in each draft, and why each shape was abandoned or kept. This is the canonical answer to "why did I give up the braid?"; the Events hold the detail of each decision.

## Summary

> [!abstract]
> Draft 1 was linear and Nell's alone; the storm came too late and Nell could not carry the town. Draft 2 was a braid of three viewpoints opening on the storm; it spent the storm's suspense early and scattered Tobias's war. Draft 3 is chronological with three viewpoints, Constance in letters, and a four-page storm prologue, which Callum still opposes.

## The three drafts

## Draft 1: linear, Nell only

Written from February to December 2025. One viewpoint seemed honest: Nell at the telegraph office hears everything that comes into the town by wire, so she could be its ear. In practice she had to be moved into rooms she had no business in, the lifeboat house, the chapel vestry, the inquiry, and the book bent around her. [[wendy-farrant]] put it as "listening at keyholes" in October 2025 ([[wendy-farrant-lunch-2025-10-08]]).

Why it changed: [[imogen-editorial-letter-2026-01-30|Imogen's letter of 30 January 2026]]. The storm, which is what the book is about, came at about 74% of the way through; Nell alone could not carry the town. Callum and Teodora had said the same.

## Draft 2: the braid

Decided on the [[editorial-call-2026-02-19|editorial call of 19 February 2026]]. Open on the storm night, then three strands moving forward from 1924, one per viewpoint, with storm-night sections recurring between them; the strands meet at the memorial. Chapter order in [[braided-chapter-map]] (archived).

What it got right: three viewpoints gave the town its width. Constance's chapters became letters, the best change of the whole process ([[constance-leal]], [[letter-chapters]]).

Why it changed, from the [[draft-two-review-2026-07-08|review of 8 July 2026]]:

1. Telling the storm first drained its suspense. Readers had the storm in pieces five times before it arrived in full, and worked out who was on the boat. See [[suspense-versus-surprise]].
2. Readers lost track of Tobias's war. Memories of 1916 and 1917 arrived inside 1925 chapters inside a 1927 frame; two readers at Larkspur & Venn gave up on his timeline, and [[tariq-mansour-continuity-notes-2026-06-30|Tariq's continuity check]] found four contradictions in his dates.
3. It was about 6,000 words longer than draft 1, mostly in connective tissue between strands.

## Draft 3: chronological, with a prologue

Planned on 2026-07-13 ([[third-draft-plan-2026-07-13]], [[third-draft-chapter-map]]). Three parts: 1924 to 1926, 1927, 1928 to 1929. Nell and Tobias alternate in close third; a Constance letter closes each run of chapters. Tobias's war returns in two whole remembered scenes. The storm opening is cut to a four-page prologue that stops as the boat clears the harbour and names no one ([[storm-prologue]]).

Still open: [[callum-pryce]] holds that any storm prologue tells the reader the boat is lost and turns parts one and two into waiting ([[should-the-salt-choir-keep-the-storm-prologue]]). Imogen and I disagree; the test is first readers. Teodora, after part one, said she read it "waiting for the boat", which both sides have claimed as evidence.

## What the history teaches me

- Diagnoses from readers were right every time; my cures were half right ([[editors-diagnose-better-than-they-prescribe]]).
- A structure has to be judged by reading it cold, not by how well it plans ([[structure-serves-the-reader-not-the-writer]]).
- The cost in time was about five months, which moved delivery to 2027-03-31 ([[delivery-date-extension]]).
